title: Impact of the novel CYP2C:TG haplotype and CYP2B6 variants on sertraline exposure in a large patient population
authors: Bråten LS, Ingelman-Sundberg M, Jukic MM, Molden E, Kringen MK
population: Adults genotyped between 2017 and 2020 with steady-state serum sertraline measurements in the therapeutic drug monitoring database of Diakonhjemmet Hospital, Oslo, treated in primary and secondary care across Norway
funder: The project was partly funded by the South-Eastern Norway Regional Health Authority, the European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation program U-PGx (grant agreement 668353) and the Swedish Research Council (grant 2021-02732). Open access funding enabled and organized by ProjektDEAL.
authorConflicts: The authors declared no competing interests for this work.
result: Against CYP2B6*1/*1 (n=454), serum sertraline was 25% higher in patients homozygous for CYP2B6*6 or *9 (n=40) and 15% higher in heterozygous carriers (n=261), and 17.4% lower in carriers of CYP2B6*4 (n=37). CYP2C19 poor metabolisers (n=29) had 2.3-fold higher concentrations than CYP2C19*1/*1. Predicted concentration with combined CYP2C19 and CYP2B6 poor metaboliser phenotypes was 2.89-fold (95% CI 2.02 to 4.15) that of combined normal metabolisers, from 2 patients.
